title: Fermentation and Extraction of Fungal Cultures
author: Jing Xu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jipckdn

steps.title: Prepare culture media
steps.instruction: Make two types of agar media as follows: Dextrose Agar (PDA): combine 200 g potato, 20 g glucose, and enough seawater to make 1000 mL; adjust pH to 7.0. Czapek’s Agar (CZA): dissolve 30 g sucrose, 15 g agar, 0.5 g KCl, and 1 g K2HPO4 in water and bring to final volume (typically 1 L). Sterilize each medium by autoclaving before use.

steps.title: Inoculate strains on PDA plates
steps.instruction: Place fungal strain inoculum onto sterile Petri dishes containing PDA medium, spread evenly, and incubate the plates at 28 °C for 5 days.

steps.title: Transfer agar patches to flasks
steps.instruction: Cut agar patches bearing fungal growth from the PDA plates and inoculate each patch into separate Erlenmeyer flasks containing the prepared media (four different media formulations).

substeps.instruction: Add the appropriate prepared medium to each Erlenmeyer flask.
Place one agar patch into each flask.

steps.title: Stationary fermentation incubation
steps.instruction: Allow the inoculated flasks to undergo stationary fermentation at room temperature for 40 days.

steps.title: Extract cultures with ethyl acetate
steps.instruction: Harvest the fermented cultures, then extract the material twice with an equal volume of ethyl acetate (EtOAc) each time; combine the extracts and evaporate the solvent to dryness to obtain the crude extract.

substeps.instruction: Add EtOAc equal to the culture volume and mix thoroughly.
Separate the organic phase, repeat the extraction with a second equal volume of EtOAc.
Combine both EtOAc extracts and evaporate under reduced pressure to dryness.
